added: #Launder towels, washcloths, and rugs. Gather any dirty towels, washcloths, and machine-washable bathmats, and launder them according to their care label; usually, towels should be washed on a cold, delicate cycle to keep them nice and fluffy.<ref>https://www.nytimes.com/wirecutter/guides/how-to-clean-your-towels/</ref> This way, they’ll be washed while you’re working on the bathroom, so they’ll be nice and clean when you get done.[[Image:Clean a Bathroom Step 2 Version 5.jpg|center]]

#Disinfect high-touch areas. Only disinfect surfaces once you’ve finished cleaning. Apply disinfectant spray to areas that are touched frequently or are especially dirty, like cabinet and faucet handles, door knobs, and the toilet seat and handle. Use disinfecting wipes to wipe anywhere there’s been oversplash on the floor or walls near the toilet.<ref>https://www.tsbvi.edu/independent-living-library/skills/cleaning-a-toilet</ref>[[Image:Clean a Bathroom Step 10 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Restock and reorganize your bathroom. Once everything has been cleaned, go ahead and put things like shampoo, toothpaste, and bathmats back where they belong. This is also a good time to empty the bathroom trash can, refill soap dispensers, and make sure toilet paper and other necessities are well-stocked.[[Image:Clean a Bathroom Step 11 Version 5.jpg|center]]

#Wash your shower curtains and liners. Because they’re exposed to moisture, shower curtains and liners can become moldy and full of bacteria. While you don’t have to wash them every time you clean your shower, aim to clean them at least once a month. In general, [[Clean-a-Shower-Curtain|wash your shower curtain]] (plastic or fabric) in the washing machine, but check the manufacturer’s instructions to be sure.<ref>https://www.cleanipedia.com/gb/bathroom-cleaning/how-to-clean-bathroom-accessories.html</ref>[[Image:Clean a Bathroom Step 12 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Scrub tile and grout. Depending on the conditions of your bathroom, it’s best to scrub tile every month or so, while [[Clean-Bathroom-Grout|grout]] only needs to be cleaned 3 or 4 times a year. [[Clean-Bathroom-Tile|Scrub your tile]] with your preferred [https://www.amazon.com/s?k=tile+and+grout+cleaner&crid=2M49AAK9ZVW47&sprefix=tile+and+grout+cleane%2Caps%2C110&ref=nb_sb_noss_2&tag=wikihow18201-20 tile and grout cleaner], and dip a [https://www.amazon.com/s?k=grout+brush&crid=3IGUBE11NUWX6&sprefix=grout+brush%2Caps%2C114&ref=nb_sb_noss_1&tag=wikihow18201-20 grout brush] into bleach to clean any discolored areas. Turn on your exhaust fan and leave the bathroom door open to keep the room ventilated.<ref>https://www.cleanipedia.com/gb/bathroom-cleaning/how-to-clean-bathroom-grout.html</ref>[[Image:Clean a Bathroom Step 13 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Descale your showerhead. If it seems like your showerhead is clogged, it’s probably time to [[Clean-the-Showerhead-with-Vinegar|descale it with vinegar]]. Fill a plastic bag about a third of the way full with distilled white vinegar and water. Use rubber bands to attach it to your showerhead so it's submerged in the vinegar and let it sit overnight. The next day, remove the bag, scrub the water holes with an old toothbrush to remove any remaining build-up, then run water through the showerhead.<ref>https://www.bhg.com/homekeeping/house-cleaning/tips/how-to-clean-a-showerhead/</ref>[[Image:Clean a Bathroom Step 14 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Clean under the toilet hinges. Dirt and debris easily get trapped in the toilet hinges, and while it’s possible to remove some of it by cleaning around the hinges, you’ll need to [[Remove-a-Toilet-Seat|remove the seat]] completely to deep clean the area. After removing the seat, spray the hinges with a disinfectant cleaner and use an old toothbrush to scrub the crevices. If your hinges have removable caps, take them off for a deeper clean.<ref>https://www.housedigest.com/442575/you-probably-didnt-know-the-toilet-seat-in-your-home-could-do-this/</ref>[[Image:Clean a Bathroom Step 15 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Remove soap scum. Cleaning your bathroom regularly should help [[Prevent-Soap-Scum|prevent soap scum]], but if it's built up, make a cleaning solution of distilled white vinegar, warm water, and a squirt of dish soap. Spray or wipe it over glass shower doors or any other surface that has soap scum. Let it sit for about half an hour, then wipe it away. Finish up with a glass cleaner to remove any remaining streaks.<Ref>https://www.cleanipedia.com/gb/bathroom-cleaning/how-to-remove-soap-scum-from-your-shower.html</ref> [[Image:Clean a Bathroom Step 16 Version 3.jpg|center]]

Get your bathroom squeaky clean with these tips
Cleaning the bathroom may sound like a chore, but it isn’t as daunting as it seems if you do so regularly. For this article, we interviewed cleaning experts Susan Stocker, Eduardo Peralta, and Filip Boksa to teach you how to properly clean every surface in your bathroom. Plus, we’ll provide tips on monthly deep cleaning, keeping your bathroom spotless between cleanings, and cleaning product recommendations.
==How do I clean the bathroom?==

#Launder towels, washcloths, and rugs. Gather any dirty towels, washcloths, and machine-washable bathmats, and launder them according to their care label; usually, towels should be washed on a cold, delicate cycle to keep them nice and fluffy.<ref>https://www.nytimes.com/wirecutter/guides/how-to-clean-your-towels/</ref> This way, they’ll be washed while you’re working on the bathroom, so they’ll be nice and clean when you get done.
#*Wipe down in-tub bathmats with some soap and water and set them aside to air dry while you work.

#Dust and vacuum from top to bottom. Using a duster or microfiber cloth, begin dusting all surfaces from the top of your bathroom down. This includes your light fixtures, windows and blinds, countertops, the outside of your toilet, and the baseboards. Vacuum any bathmats or rugs to remove excess dust and debris.https://www.southernliving.com/how-to-clean-a-bathroom-8695839

{{whvid|Clean a Bathroom Step 3 Version 2.360p.mp4|Clean a Bathroom Step 3-preview Version 2.jpg|Clean a Bathroom Step 3 Version 4.jpg|gif=Clean a Bathroom Step 3 Version 2.360p.gif|giffirst=Clean a Bathroom Step 3 Version 2.360p.first.gif}}

#*If your mirror is particularly cloudy, Boksa says, “The easiest way to clean a cloudy mirror is to fill a spray-bottle with white vinegar and apply it to the glass. Wipe off the vinegar with a lint-free rag for a perfect finish. Be careful not to spray vinegar onto the wooden frame if present.”<ref>[v161127_b01]. 20 August 2019.</ref>

#*If your sink is ceramic, Stocker suggests using baking soda to clean it: “Make sure you get it mixed with enough water to make a paste or it’s not going to work—it requires the power of scrubbing just as much as it requires the power of baking soda.  [Baking soda] has just the right amount of abrasive power to lift and remove dirt and grease, but it is not going to remove stubborn stains.”<ref>[v161131_b03]. 8 November 2019.</ref>

#*For large, tough stains, Peralta says, “Apply [an acidic toilet bowl cleaner] to the entire bowl of the toilet and let sit for about 10 minutes, then scrub [with a toilet brush] and flush to rinse. Apply bleach spray to the entire toilet bowl, let sit for 5 minutes, then use pumice to give it a good hard scrub. A magic eraser may be used as well to brighten the area.”<ref>[v162005_b01]. 29 October 2021.</ref>

#*When using bleach, Peralta says, “Always use protective eyewear, gloves, and [a] mask. I highly recommend opening windows, and never mix bleach with anything other than water, as this may cause chemical burns and dangerous fumes.”<ref>[v162005_b01]. 29 October 2021.</ref>
===How to Deep Clean Your Bathroom Monthly{{sa_no_numbers:}}{{toc_item:Monthly Deep Cleaning}}===

#Wash your shower curtains and liners. Because they’re exposed to moisture, shower curtains and liners can become moldy and full of bacteria. While you don’t have to wash them every time you clean your shower, aim to clean them at least once a month. In general, [[Clean-a-Shower-Curtain|wash your shower curtain]] (plastic or fabric) in the washing machine, but check the manufacturer’s instructions to be sure.<ref>https://www.cleanipedia.com/gb/bathroom-cleaning/how-to-clean-bathroom-accessories.html</ref>

#Wipe down the shower after you use it. To prevent and [[Remove-Bathroom-Mold|remove mold]] and mildew, wipe your bathtub and shower down every time you take a shower to remove excess moisture. Combined with running the fan, this should keep your bathroom mildew free.https://www.cleaninginstitute.org/cleaning-tips/clean-home/room-room/bathroom-cleaning-tips

{{whvid|Clean a Bathroom Step 14 Version 2.360p.mp4|Clean a Bathroom Step 14-preview Version 2.jpg|Clean a Bathroom Step 14 Version 2.jpg|gif=Clean a Bathroom Step 14 Version 2.360p.gif|giffirst=Clean a Bathroom Step 14 Version 2.360p.first.gif}}

#Powerstone Pumice Stone Toilet Bowl Cleaner{endbold} The [https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Powerstone+Pumice+Stone+Toilet+Bowl+Cleaner+with+Handle&crid=1Z9OAFNKQU2YW&sprefix=powerstone+pumice+stone+toilet+bowl+cleaner+with+handle%2Caps%2C208&ref=nb_sb_noss_1&##affiliate_article_id## Powerstone Pumice Stone Toilet Bowl Cleaner with Handle] effectively removes rings and calcium build-up from your toilet without scratching the bowl. Simply wet the stone, then lightly scrub the toilet until the stains are removed. You will need a disinfectant product to kill germs, however.<Ref>https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/home/cleaning/g19746417/best-toilet-bowl-cleaners/</ref>

*Mix a cleaning solution of water and a bit of bleach in a spray bottle and spray it on hard-to-reach mildew spots (like on the ceiling) to eliminate them.<Ref>https://www.bobvila.com/articles/mold-on-ceiling/</ref>
*If you aren’t able or don’t want to clean your bathroom yourself, consider hiring a professional cleaning service to keep your bathroom hygienic.

added: ==Quick Summary==

To clean a bathroom, remove all items from the counters and shelves, and place them outside of the bathroom. Open the doors and turn on the ventilation fan if you have one, and then pour bleach into the toilet bowl with the cleaning brush in the bowl to sanitize it. Dust the room to remove cobwebs, and spray bathroom cleaner on all of the surfaces, including the shower, sink, and exterior of the toilet. Clean each area with its own designated sponge or towel to prevent the spread of germs. Scrub the toilet bowl and flush before sweeping and mopping the floor.

== Tips ==

*Rinse your sponge or scrub brush numerous times as you go along, and change your mop water when it gets dirty. The object of cleaning is to wash dirt away and down a drain, not to move it around your bathroom.
* Wear rubber gloves to maintain hygiene.

*There are a lot of tiny nooks and crannies you can't get a sponge or rag into. A number of cotton swabs can be helpful, as can a toothbrush (kept only for cleaning, of course!) for getting into all kinds of tricky corners and between tiles.

===Preparing to Clean===

#Remove all the items that don't belong in your bathroom. Take out everything that doesn't belong, such as clothes, cups, and trash. Also move out any little side tables or movable storage cabinets so that you can clean under them.

[[Image:Clean a Bathroom Step 1 Version 2.jpg|center|550px]]

#Pour some bleach or another disinfectant into the toilet bowl. Put the toilet brush inside the bowl, helping to sanitize the brush for cleaning.

[[Image:Clean a Bathroom Step 2 Version 2.jpg|center|550px]]
#*Make sure the floor is open and the fan is on to ensure proper ventilation.
#*For a green alternative, mix a tablespoon of baking powder into about a quart of 75/25 mix of white vinegar and water.

#Dust. In general, when cleaning any room, start from the top down. Clean cobwebs in the corners of the bathroom, and brush other dust and dirt directly onto the floor to sweep up later. A duster works great for this, but you can also use the broom.
#*If you've got delicate wallpaper, wrap the bristles in some toilet paper or paper towel and slightly wet it to

#Apply any scrub powder to especially dirty areas. If you've got lime and build-up in the tub, sink, or around faucets, damp those areas slightly and sprinkle with scrubbing powder like Comet. Letting it sit for 10-15 minutes while you do other things will help to work loose the dirty patches and make your scrubbing go much more smoothly.
#*Be sure to read the label and ensure that you're using an appropriate product and won't damage your surfaces. Test it  out on a non-visible spot before you actually use it.
===Cleaning Surfaces===

#Clean the walls, windows and/or ceiling. If you have mold on the ceiling start with spraying a water bleach/disinfectant solution on it and let it rest for a couple of minutes, do the same with the walls ( if they are tiles) or use another cleaning product. With a sponge or a clean rag, scrub the tile surfaces you've sprayed. Rinse it carefully to avoid any stripes and dry it with a clean rag.

[[Image:Clean a Bathroom Step 4 Version 2.jpg|center|550px]]
#*It's a good idea to wear rubber gloves while you're scrubbing, to keep your hands from drying out if you're using harsh products.

#Clean the shower. Spray cleaning product on the shower walls, and the shower head and let it rest for a couple of minutes. Spray cleansers made especially for getting rid of soap scum work very well on tubs that haven't been cleaned in a while.

[[Image:Clean a Bathroom Step 6 Version 2.jpg|center|550px]]

#*For hard water areas that are prone to green and rust-colored stains, a cleanser made for eliminating calcium, lime and rust is probably what you need. Never use abrasive cleaners or green abrasive scrub pads or steel wool on porcelain fixtures, as they will quickly dull the finish.

#*Soak the showerhead. If eventually the showerhead becomes quite clogged with hard water build up or soap scum, you can remove it and soak it overnight in a vinegar/water mixture, and then clean with a toothbrush.

#*Go back over the shower and scrub the walls, faucet and shower head, rinse well with the hottest water and or dry with a towel. You can shine the faucet with a paper towel or a towel.

[[Image:Clean a Bathroom Step 6Bullet1.jpg|center|550px]]

#*Don't forget the shower curtain; it is also prone to mildew. A solution of about 2/3 water, 1/3 bleach in a spray bottle can be handy for getting rid of mildew spots. Or you can take it down and wash it in hot water with a small amount of soap and bleach.

[[Image:Clean a Bathroom Step 6Bullet2.jpg|center|550px]]

#Clean the sink and counter area. Scrub all the soap scum and tooth paste off with a small amount of cleaner, rinsing your sponge thoroughly as you go along.http://www.apartmenttherapy.com/keeping-your-bathroom-clean-in-5-minutes-a-day-171474 An old toothbrush or cotton swabs can be handy for getting the junk out from between the tap and handles.

[[Image:Clean a Bathroom Step 7 Version 2.jpg|center|550px]]

#*Be sure never to clean the sink and counter area with the same rag or paper towel you used to clean the toilet. This can spread leftover disease-causing germs to your sink and counter area. To prevent this you can use a specific rag which you use to clean only the toilet.

#*Wipe off the fronts and tops of cabinets and drawers. You'll probably want to use hot, soapy water for this purpose. If you're worried about germs on these surfaces, add a bit of bleach to your soapy water.

#Clean the mirror. Use cleaner, rinse it and wipe the excessive water off with a towel or squeegee. To add a shine to your mirror add a bit vinegar to the water.

[[Image:Clean a Bathroom Step 7Bullet2 Version 2.jpg|center|550px]]

#Clean the exterior of the toilet. Wipe the outside, starting with the flush handle so as not to re-contaminate it, with a cloth soaked in disinfectant cleaner. Thoroughly wash and rinse all exterior surfaces of the toilet bowl, including the underside and flared base, the top and underside of the seat and lid, and the hinges and their mounting area with a cloth and detergent or similar cleaner.

[[Image:Clean a Bathroom Step 8 Version 2.jpg|center|550px]]
#*Don't forget to use a cloth specially assigned for cleaning the toilet, or a paper towel (throw it away, don't flush it).

#Scrub the bowl with a toilet brush and flush. You probably won't have to scrub hard: let the soapy water and patience dissolve the problem. Coat the inside of the bowl  with a viscous acidic cleaner generally sold in an angle-necked bottle. Take special care to cover the entire inside edge of the rim; it'll run down toward other areas.<ref>http://www.marthastewart.com/275312/vacuum-any-surface/@center/277000/homekeeping-solutions</ref>

#*Allow the cleaner to soak for half an hour or more before scrubbing the entire bowl including under the rim with a toilet bowl brush, let it soak a little longer after it's been well-distributed though thinned by the initial scrubbing, then scrub some more and flush it away.

#Sweep and mop the floor. Start with the farthest point from the door. Sweep up all the dust and debris you've cleaned so far and let fall on the floor, then mop using hot soapy bleach water. Remember to rinse the floor with clean water to remove slippery soap residue. Be sure to get along the sides of your toilet bowl where it is anchored to the floor. This area is notoriously dirty. Don't forget to clean the base boards or base molds these places usually accumulates a lot of dust.

[[Image:Clean a Bathroom Step 9 Version 2.jpg|center|550px]]
===Keeping the Bathroom Clean===

#Run the fan. Keeping your bathroom ventilated will discourage the growth of mildew, keeping your big cleaning sessions few and far between. Always run the fan after you get out of the shower, to dry out the bathroom and keep the moisture from clinging.

#Wipe down the shower after you use it. To make sure mold and mildew doesn't build up in the shower in between big cleaning sessions, take time to wipe it down every time you take a shower. Combined  with running the fan, this should keep your bathroom mildew free.

#Keep it tidy. Much of what we call "mess" is really just clutter. If clothes accumulate in your bathroom, put a hamper, or even a cardboard box in the bathroom to collect dirty clothes. Use a toothbrush holder or a cup to keep your toothbrushes in order. Keep other supplies in an old shoebox under the sink to keep the surface tidy.

#Use the toilet brush. Even if it doesn't look dirty, minerals in the water can stain the bowl, so it's a good idea to brush the toilet down with a sturdy toilet brush fairly regularly. If you do this even just once a week, your bigger cleanings will be much easier and infrequent.

#Wash toothpaste down. Toothpaste stains and build up in the sink and even on the mirror can make a bathroom look dirtier than it needs to be. Make sure you clean up after your toothpaste, washing it down and rinsing the sink out, then drying the bowl of the sink when you're finished.
#*To consolidate tasks, do this while you mouthwash for an added dental benefit.

*There are a lot of tiny nooks and crannies you can't get a sponge or rag into. A number of cotton swabs can be helpful, as can a toothbrush (kept only for cleaning, of course!) for getting into all kinds of tricky corners and between tiles.
*Don't ever mix bleach and ammonia! Even sponges that have formerly come in contact with bleach can react with ammonia and cause ''poisonous'' chlorine gas to form.

== Video ==
{{Video:Clean a Bathroom|}}
== Tips ==

*There are a lot of tiny nooks and crannies you can't get a sponge or rag into.  A number of cotton swabs can be helpful, as can a toothbrush (kept only for cleaning, of course!) for getting into all kinds of tricky corners and between tiles.
*Calcium-lime-rust eliminating cleansers can also be sprayed on your shower head to unclog hard-water buildup and regain water pressure. For best results, spray a few times a week after showering.
*Remember: the number one enemy of mildew is bleach. Often just a small application of bleach will eliminate mildew stains without the need for scrubbing.
*Rubber gloves will spare your hands.
*A squeegee will get glass surfaces looking really clean without water spots.
*Ventilate your bathroom while cleaning. Fumes are never good for you.

*Rinse your sponge or scrub brush numerous times as you go along, and change your mop water when it gets dirty. The object of cleaning is to wash dirt away and down a drain, not to move it around your bathroom.

*Once your tub has been thoroughly cleaned as per the above instructions, a no-rinse tub and shower cleaner (Tilex makes such a product in the US) that you apply after each shower can be used to maintain your tub or shower's cleanliness with little effort.

*Don't forget to clean the ceiling. A bleach-water solution in a spray bottle can be used to eliminate mildew spots on the ceiling as well.

*Wear old clothes that you don't mind getting dirty.
*'''Don't ever mix bleach and ammonia! Even sponges that have formerly come in contact with bleach can react with ammonia and cause ''poisonous'' chlorine gas to form.'''

*Be careful while using cleaning products.

*Toilet-bowl cleaner is strongly acidic and more dangerous than most cleaning products.  Restrict its use to cleaning a toilet bowl with a toilet brush.  Don't squirt it in the direction of, and try not to spatter it near, your face.
== Things You'll Need ==
*Sponge, Squeegee, or scrub brush
*Vacuum
*Broom (rubber-bristle or regular)
*Dustpan
*Bleach
*Toilet cleanser and toilet brush
*General-purpose bathroom cleanser (spray or powder)
*Bucket
*Mop (optional; a small bathroom can be mopped by hand with a sponge)
*Cloths
*Paper towels
*Glass cleanser
*Rubber gloves
*Spray bottle
*Dish soap or laundry detergent
*Steel wool (optional)
*Toothbrush or cotton swabs (optional)
